findings.where: electron/lib/autonomyGate.cjs — normalise()/trimSegments() and namesGovernedPath(), consumed by inspectCreate at both origins and by upgradeApplier.applyWith step 3; and electron/lib/upgradeApplier.cjs — validatePath(), which resolves for confinement but never rejects a stream spelling
findings.problem: An NTFS stream suffix is not canonicalised, so a path that IS a governed file reads as naming nothing governed. On NTFS, "file::$DATA" is a synonym for the primary data stream. Measured end to end on this platform against a scratch repo fixture with the real policy, capability and loyaltyGuard modules: gate.namesGovernedPath('electron/lib/autonomyStop.cjs::$DATA') returns null; path.resolve keeps the suffix so the confinement check passes; lstatSync reports a regular file; readFileSync through the spelling returns the real file's bytes so the baseSha256 base-drift check PASSES rather than catching it; and a master-approved self-upgrade patch with action 'patch' APPLIED, leaving electron/lib/autonomyStop.cjs containing "function isStopped(){return false;}". The same spelling replaced shared/loyalty-tripwire.json with {"approved":"everything"} — the tamper-evidence baseline the loyalty tripwire compares against — and carried a patch of electron/lib/loyaltyGuard.cjs through the applier's step 2 with guard.inspectChanges returning {ok:true,refused:[]}. This is the THIRD spelling in three review rounds that this fence has failed to canonicalise (round 1: unresolved structure; round 2: trailing dot and space) and the FIRST whose governed bytes do not survive — round 2's was graded NIT precisely because the bytes did survive. In-scope item 1, "the STOP unreachable by any proposal", is therefore false for this design's own kind. Bounds, so the severity is not overstated: I6 is intact (the apply still needs master's recorded approval, and proposals.apply has no in-process caller in this design); the create fence refuses the owned kinds at origin 'ipc' so a renderer cannot file one; fileProposal has no caller and the five-stage authoring loop is deferred, so nothing in the shipped tree constructs such a change. The loyaltyGuard blind spot itself is PRE-EXISTING (proposals.create already feeds it unnormalised paths and loyaltyGuard.cjs is protected), but the applier's step 2 is new code presented as the covenant re-run rather than trusted, and for this spelling it refuses nothing. A true alternate stream (':evil') writes a hidden stream and leaves the primary intact; a trailing tab fails ENOENT on this platform with nothing clobbered — same gap, no impact today.
findings.fix: Two places, both small. (1) In upgradeApplier.validatePath, refuse the spelling class outright before resolving: reject any change path whose segments contain a ':' other than a leading drive designator (/^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]/), and reject any path containing a control character (/[\u0000-\u001f]/). A stream or control-character name is never a legitimate source file, so a plain refusal naming the path is correct and the revert path is never entered for it. (2) In autonomyGate.normalise, strip a stream suffix per segment (seg.split(':')[0] after the drive prefix is accounted for) alongside the existing trailing dot/space trim, so namesGovernedPath REPORTS the path as governed at both origins and at the applier's step 3 rather than relying solely on validatePath. Then extend the variants() generator in scripts/verifyUpgradeApplier.cjs §13 — which already runs seven spellings x four governed paths x every gate with an ungoverned control — with '::$DATA', ':stream' and a trailing '\t', asserting for each that inspectCreate refuses at both origins, that applyWith refuses, AND that the governed file's bytes are byte-identical afterwards (the bytes assertion is the one that would have caught this). Add one row for a protected file via the same spelling so the step-2 claim is held too.
